title: Lord Howe Island's clocks only move 30 minutes for daylight saving, not an hour
assumption: Daylight saving time always shifts the clock by exactly one hour.

input.display: ZoneInfo("Australia/Lord_Howe") offset: +10:30 in southern winter (July), +11:00 in southern summer (January)
input.description: Any scheduling code that assumes 'DST offset == standard offset +/- 60 minutes' and uses that to detect or compute DST transitions.

what_goes_wrong: Code that infers 'is this a DST transition' by checking whether the offset changed by exactly 60 minutes misses Lord Howe Island's transitions (and misclassifies the island's clock change as a data error).
why: Australia/Lord_Howe is currently the only zone in the tz database whose DST shift is 30 minutes: standard time is UTC+10:30, and daylight time is UTC+11:00, a half-hour step instead of the usual hour. The IANA tz database encodes this per-zone; there is no general rule that DST is always 60 minutes, so hardcoding that assumption breaks for this zone even though every API used (zoneinfo, Intl) reports the real offset correctly. (DST shifts of other sizes exist too: Antarctica/Troll moves two hours.)

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime

tz = ZoneInfo("Australia/Lord_Howe")
summer = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=tz)  # DST active (southern summer)
winter = datetime(2024, 7, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=tz)  # standard time
print("DST offset:", summer.utcoffset(), "dst() component:", summer.dst())
print("standard offset:", winter.utcoffset(), "dst() component:", winter.dst())
print("shift between the two, in minutes:", (summer.utcoffset() - winter.utcoffset()).total_seconds() / 60)
repros.expected_output:
DST offset: 11:00:00 dst() component: 0:30:00
standard offset: 10:30:00 dst() component: 0:00:00
shift between the two, in minutes: 30.0

fix: Never hardcode the size of a DST shift. Ask the timezone library for the actual UTC offset at each instant and diff those; don't assume +/-60 minutes anywhere in validation or transition-detection logic.
